identity.name: Kingdom of Liaodong (Eighteen Kingdoms)
alt_names: Kingdom of Liaodong under Xiang Yu

land.text: southern Liaoning, 'Part of the former Yan kingdom' granted to Han Guang

predecessors.note: Zang Tu page: 'Part of the former Yan kingdom was granted to Han Guang, who was appointed by Xiang Yu as the King of Liaodong.' The yan dossier (ea-01) records the matching split.

land.text: Liaodong, taken when Zang Tu killed Han Guang

successors.note: Zang Tu page: he 'killed him at Wuzhong, thereby becoming king of a united Yan kingdom'.

capitals.name: Wuzhong (Ji County, Tianjin)
capitals.note: Chinese Wikipedia, 韓廣: Han Guang was moved to be King of Liaodong '以無終(今天津薊縣)為都' in 206, refused to go ('不肯遷往遼東') and was killed by Zang Tu the same year. Wuzhong lies about 160 km west of Cliopatria's Liaodong shape (west edge 119.26 E), inside Cliopatria's Yan 206 shape (reviewer, 2026-10-19). Wuzhong is not in the gazetteer.

rulers.name: Han Guang
rulers.note: Page: 'Han Guang (died 206 BC)'; infobox King of Yan 209-206 BC and King of Liaodong 206 BC.

correction.text: unchanged outline, but only for 206: Zang Tu killed Han Guang and united Yan and Liaodong

keyframe_review.note: 70,288 km2, bbox 119.3-124.8 E, 38.7-41.9 N: the Liaodong Peninsula, the table's 'southern Liaoning'. No page opened gives an area, so no infobox figure to compare. Cliopatria keeps the row to 204; the Timeline and Han Guang pages put Han Guang's death in 206, so the cells go to Yan (Zang Tu) from 206. The Eighteen Kingdoms table's 'Surrendered to Liu Bang' contradicts the Zang Tu page and is not followed. Reviewer 2026-10-19: the capital Wuzhong (Chinese Wikipedia, 韓廣: '以無終(今天津薊縣)為都') lies about 160 km west of this outline, inside Cliopatria's Yan 206 shape; the outline is kept because Han Guang refused to go to Liaodong ('不肯遷往遼東') and was killed the same year.

region.text: southern Liaoning (Eighteen Kingdoms table), the Liaodong Peninsula that Xiang Yu gave Han Guang

ledger.note: 206: Xiang Yu splits Liaodong from Yan and makes Han Guang its king. Table: 'Liaodong (遼東): Han Guang (Yan royalty); southern Liaoning'; kingdoms 'created by military leader Xiang Yu in 206 BCE'. The Han Guang page: 'He granted Han Guang the title of King of Liaodong (遼東王) and relocated Han Guang to the Liaodong Peninsula.'

region.text: southern Liaoning (Eighteen Kingdoms table), the Liaodong Peninsula that Xiang Yu gave Han Guang

ledger.note: 206: Zang Tu, King of Yan, kills Han Guang and takes Liaodong. 'Zang Tu, the King of Yan, kills Han Guang, the King of Liaodong.' The Zang Tu page: Han Guang 'refused to comply. As a result, Zang Tu attacked Han Guang and killed him at Wuzhong, thereby becoming king of a united Yan kingdom'; the Han Guang page dates his death to 206. The land passing to Yan is the Zang Tu page's 'united Yan kingdom'; no month on any page.

region.text: southern Liaoning (Eighteen Kingdoms table), the Liaodong Peninsula that Xiang Yu gave Han Guang

ledger.note: 206: the Kingdom of Liaodong ends in the same year it began. Date and successor as for the loss; the yan dossier records the matching gain in 206.

wars.name: Zang Tu's conquest of Liaodong

zones.text: Liaodong, where Zang Tu defeated and killed Han Guang

wars.outcome: Yan (Zang Tu) victory: Zang Tu 'killed him at Wuzhong, thereby becoming king of a united Yan kingdom' (Zang Tu page); the Timeline page puts 'Zang Tu, the King of Yan, kills Han Guang, the King of Liaodong' under 206 BC.
wars.note: The Zang Tu page gives no year for the killing; the Timeline and Han Guang pages give 206. Zang Tu himself rebelled against Han in 202 and was captured about October (Zang Tu page). Reviewer 2026-10-19: renamed from 'Chu–Han Contention' (206-202) and limited to 206, since the war that ended Liaodong was Zang Tu's, not the Chu-Han war.

certainty.note: The kingdom was assigned by Xiang Yu from the old Yan; no survey or treaty lines; the outline is Cliopatria's approximation.

notes:
Wikidata Q5349053 is the Eighteen Kingdoms item shared by twelve Cliopatria rows; Liaodong is its own kingdom (Han Guang), so it keeps its own dossier.
The Eighteen Kingdoms table says Liaodong 'Surrendered to Liu Bang'; the Zang Tu, Han Guang and Timeline pages say Zang Tu killed Han Guang in 206 and the yan dossier agrees. The kingdom is therefore cut to 206, the Cliopatria row (to 204) notwithstanding. The Cliopatria Yan row for 206-204 (42,088 km2, bbox 116.0-119.8 E, 38.7-40.7 N) does not include the Liaodong Peninsula, so the compiler must add the Liaodong cells to Yan from 206 as the yan ledger's gain says.
Capital and location of Wuzhong are unverified; list Wuzhong in the gazetteer. The Han Guang page is silent on Ji/Jicheng, Wuzhong and any month.
